rules.title: Model follows a star schema with distinct fact and dimension tables
rules.requirement: AI-facing semantic models must use a star schema with clearly separated fact and dimension tables; flat denormalized tables and pivoted structures must be avoided.
rules.rationale: Named as the primary structural pitfall: non-star schemas make efficient DAX harder to write correctly, so the generator produces inefficient or wrong queries. This is the single largest structural driver of the broad-scan behaviour.

check.how: Review the relationship graph. Flag snowflaked chains, fact-to-fact relationships, and wide flat tables carrying both measures and descriptive attributes.

rules.remediation: Refactor into conformed dimensions and narrow fact tables. Unpivot wide tables so each row is one observation.
rules.impactIfViolated: Inefficient generated DAX, longer scans, higher CU burn per question, and lower answer accuracy.

rules.title: Relationships are defined with explicit, correct cardinality
rules.requirement: Every relationship between AI-visible tables must exist and declare the correct cardinality - one-to-many, many-to-one, or many-to-many - and the correct filter direction.
rules.rationale: Clear relationships with specified cardinality are a stated requirement. Missing or wrong relationships force the generator to invent joins, which is where fabricated numbers come from.

check.how: Enumerate relationships via INFO.RELATIONSHIPS(). Flag missing joins between AI-visible fact and dimension tables, and any many-to-many not deliberately intended.

rules.remediation: Define the missing relationships and correct cardinality. Replace incidental many-to-many with a bridge dimension.
rules.impactIfViolated: Cross-joins, inflated totals, and answers that cannot be reconciled to any report.

rules.title: Ambiguous relationship paths are eliminated
rules.requirement: The model must not contain ambiguous relationship paths between AI-visible tables.
rules.rationale: Explicitly listed among the practices to follow. Where two paths connect the same tables, the generator's choice is not predictable and neither are the results.

check.how: Trace the relationship graph for multiple active paths between any two AI-visible tables.
check.expected: single active path per table pair

rules.remediation: Deactivate redundant relationships and expose the alternate path through an explicit measure using USERELATIONSHIP.
rules.impactIfViolated: Same question, different answer, depending on the path chosen.

rules.title: Role-playing relationships are marked inactive and surfaced through measures
rules.requirement: Role-playing dimension relationships must be marked inactive where appropriate, with active/inactive state clearly specified.
rules.rationale: Direct guidance to clearly specify active and inactive relationships and mark role-playing relationships inactive when appropriate.

check.how: For dimensions related more than once to a fact, confirm exactly one active relationship and named measures for the inactive roles.
check.expected: one active, roles exposed via measures

rules.remediation: Create measures such as Sales by Ship Date using USERELATIONSHIP, and name them so the role is obvious.
rules.impactIfViolated: Date-based questions silently resolve against the wrong date role.

rules.title: A marked date table with hierarchies exists
rules.requirement: The model must contain a dedicated date dimension with a logical drill hierarchy - Year > Quarter > Month > Day - and it must be marked as the date table.
rules.rationale: Hierarchies for drill-down are a stated structural requirement, and time intelligence in generated DAX depends on a proper date table.

check.how: Confirm a date table exists, is marked as such, is contiguous, and exposes a Year/Quarter/Month/Day hierarchy.

rules.remediation: Add and mark a conformed date dimension; remove auto date/time tables that clutter the AI-visible schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Time-intelligence questions fail or return wrong periods - the most common category of user-facing Copilot error.

rules.title: Ambiguous date columns carry explicit default guidance
rules.requirement: Where a model exposes several date columns - Order Date, Ship Date, Due Date - AI instructions or verified answers must state which is the default for each question type.
rules.rationale: Called out as a specific pitfall: multiple date columns require clear guidance or the AI is confused. Guidance is the fix, not removal.

check.how: Count AI-visible date columns; if more than one, confirm AI instructions name the default and the conditions for using the others.

rules.remediation: Add an explicit line to AI instructions, for example: unless the user names a date type, use Order Date.
rules.impactIfViolated: Revenue questions answered on ship date; the numbers look plausible and are wrong.

rules.title: Fact and dimension tables are explicitly named
rules.requirement: Tables should be named so their role is unmistakable - FactSales, FactTransactions, DimProduct, DimCustomer - or follow an equivalent consistent convention.
rules.rationale: Explicit naming guidance. Role clarity in the name reduces the reasoning the generator must do before it can plan a query.

check.how: Review AI-visible table names for a consistent, role-revealing convention.

rules.remediation: Adopt one convention and apply it uniformly. Consistency matters more than which convention you pick.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator misclassifies a dimension as a fact and aggregates attributes.

rules.title: Unused tables, columns and measures are removed
rules.requirement: Objects not required by any report or by the AI question scope must be removed from the model.
rules.rationale: Model bloat is named directly: remove unnecessary columns, tables and measures to reduce noise for the DAX generation tool. Every unused object is a candidate the generator must rule out.

check.how: Use the Semantic Model Memory Analyzer or a VPAX extract to identify unreferenced objects.

rules.remediation: Delete them, or at minimum hide and exclude them from the AI data schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Higher token cost per question and more ways for the generator to go wrong.

rules.title: Disconnected and field-parameter tables are limited
rules.requirement: Disconnected tables, including field parameter tables, must be minimized in the AI-visible schema and documented where retained.
rules.rationale: Named as an unsupported complex pattern that may cause unexpected results, alongside currency conversion patterns.

check.how: List AI-visible tables with no relationships; confirm each is deliberate and documented.

rules.remediation: Exclude field parameter tables from the AI data schema; they are a report interactivity device, not a semantic concept.
rules.impactIfViolated: Unpredictable results on any question that touches the disconnected table.

rules.title: Currency conversion patterns are flagged as unsupported
rules.requirement: Models implementing currency conversion must document that this pattern is not reliably supported and constrain the question scope accordingly.
rules.rationale: Currency conversion is explicitly listed among complex patterns that may cause unexpected results.

check.how: Identify currency conversion logic and confirm the limitation is documented and tested.

rules.remediation: Pre-compute reporting-currency measures and expose only those to the AI schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Currency-denominated answers are wrong in ways that are hard to spot.

rules.title: Explicit measures exist for every metric users will ask about
rules.requirement: Every business metric within the question scope must be implemented as an explicit DAX measure.
rules.rationale: Explicit measures are required; implicit measures lead to unpredictable results. If the metric is not a measure, the generator has to invent the aggregation.

check.how: Map each metric in the question scope to a named measure. Flag any metric with no measure.

rules.remediation: Create the measures, name them the way the business names them, and describe them.
rules.impactIfViolated: Invented aggregations that do not match the organization's official definition.

rules.title: Implicit measures are suppressed on AI-visible numeric columns
rules.requirement: Numeric columns in the AI schema must not rely on implicit aggregation where an explicit measure is the intended answer.
rules.rationale: Implicit measures are named as a pitfall producing unpredictable results. A raw numeric column adjacent to a proper measure gives the generator a wrong-but-available option.

check.how: For AI-visible numeric columns, confirm either an explicit measure covers the metric and the raw column is excluded, or the column's default summarization is deliberately set.

rules.remediation: Exclude raw fact numeric columns from the AI schema once explicit measures exist.
rules.impactIfViolated: SUM of a raw column returned where a ratio or filtered measure was correct.

rules.title: Default summarization is set correctly on numeric columns
rules.requirement: Every AI-visible numeric column must have a deliberate default summarization - Sum, Average or None - rather than the inherited default.
rules.rationale: Stated requirement, to prevent unintended aggregations. Averaging a ratio column or summing a year is the classic failure.

check.how: Read the summarizeBy property for AI-visible numeric columns. Flag ratio, percentage, year and key columns not set to None.
check.expected: deliberate summarizeBy on every numeric column

rules.remediation: Set summarizeBy to None on identifiers, years and ratios; set Sum or Average deliberately elsewhere.
rules.impactIfViolated: Summed percentages and averaged keys presented as fact.

rules.title: Helper and intermediate measures are excluded from the AI schema
rules.requirement: Only measures that calculate an actual business metric may be AI-visible; helper measures and intermediate objects used for report interactivity must be excluded.
rules.rationale: Direct instruction. Including unnecessary measures increases noise and decreases accuracy.

check.how: Classify every AI-visible measure as business metric or helper; flag helpers.

rules.remediation: Hide helper measures and exclude them from the AI data schema; keep them in a clearly named technical display folder.
rules.impactIfViolated: Answers built on formatting or selection-state helpers that were never meant to be reported.

rules.title: Near-duplicate measures are eliminated or clearly differentiated
rules.requirement: The AI schema must not expose several measures meaning approximately the same thing - Total Sales, Sales Amount, Revenue - unless each carries a description that makes the distinction explicit.
rules.rationale: Named as a pitfall creating ambiguity for DAX generation. This is one of the most common causes of two users getting two different numbers for the same question.

check.how: Cluster AI-visible measure names by semantic similarity; review each cluster for genuine distinction.

rules.remediation: Keep one canonical measure per concept. Where variants are genuinely needed, encode the distinction in the name and describe it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Inconsistent answers to the same business question, which is the fastest route to losing executive trust.

rules.title: Measures are named in business language, not technical shorthand
rules.requirement: Measure and column names must be descriptive business terms - Average Customer Rating rather than AvgRating, Total Revenue rather than TR_AMT, Sales Region rather than DIM_GEO_01.
rules.rationale: Stated with these exact examples. Abbreviations and acronyms increase error probability, and non-descriptive naming leaves the DAX tool with no context at all.

check.how: Scan AI-visible object names for abbreviations, underscores, all-caps tokens and source-system prefixes.

rules.remediation: Rename in the semantic layer. Source-system names belong in Power Query, not in the AI-visible model.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator has no basis for mapping a user's words to your fields.

rules.title: Commonly requested measures are pre-built rather than left to generation
rules.requirement: Frequently requested calculations - YTD, month-over-month growth, prior-year comparison, run rate - must exist as measures instead of relying on the generator to compose them.
rules.rationale: Guidance to include commonly requested measures users are likely to need, with YTD Sales and MoM Growth given as examples. Pre-built beats generated every time on both accuracy and cost.

check.how: Compare the top question patterns against the measure inventory; flag common patterns with no backing measure.

rules.remediation: Build the top time-intelligence and comparison measures explicitly. Each one removes a whole class of generation errors.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator writes time intelligence from scratch on every question, slowly and sometimes wrongly.

rules.title: Business KPIs are defined in the model
rules.requirement: Business-relevant KPIs such as ROI, CAC and LTV should be defined as measures where they are part of the question scope.
rules.rationale: Stated as a requirement with these examples. A KPI the business talks about but the model does not contain is a guaranteed hallucination opportunity.

check.how: Compare the business KPI catalogue to the measure inventory.

rules.remediation: Implement the KPIs with the official definitions and describe the calculation basis.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users ask for a named KPI and receive an approximation the generator assembled.

rules.title: Calculation groups carry item names in the description
rules.requirement: Every calculation group must have a description that lists and explains its calculation items, within the first 200 characters.
rules.rationale: Copilot struggles to use calculation groups; the documented mitigation is to include the calculation item names in the description, which is truncated at 200 characters.

check.how: For each calculation group, confirm the description names the items and that the essential content sits in the first 200 characters.

rules.remediation: Front-load the item names, then any explanation. Anything past character 200 is not read.
rules.impactIfViolated: Calculation groups are effectively invisible and time-intelligence answers ignore them.

rules.title: DAX comments are not used to convey meaning to Copilot
rules.requirement: Semantic context must live in descriptions, not in DAX comments.
rules.rationale: Comments in DAX expressions are explicitly excluded from grounding data. Teams document measures in comments and assume Copilot reads them.

check.how: Sample measures with substantial comment blocks and confirm the same context exists in the description.

rules.remediation: Move the business meaning into the description; keep comments for maintainers.
rules.impactIfViolated: Carefully documented measures that Copilot understands no better than undocumented ones.

rules.title: Newer DAX functions are used cautiously in AI-facing models
rules.requirement: Where a model relies on recently introduced DAX functions or syntax, the team must test AI behaviour against those measures specifically.
rules.rationale: Copilot has limited training data for newer DAX functions and syntax and may produce mistakes with them.

check.how: Identify measures using recent DAX functions and include them in the golden question set.

rules.remediation: Wrap the newer logic in a stable named measure so the generator references rather than rewrites it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Generation errors concentrated in the newest parts of the model.

rules.title: Variable-heavy measures are validated for filter and grouping behaviour
rules.requirement: Measures making heavy use of DAX variables must be tested, because Copilot may inappropriately filter or group on already-declared variables.
rules.rationale: Named as a specific known failure mode.

check.how: Include variable-heavy measures in the golden question set and inspect the generated DAX.

rules.remediation: Simplify the public-facing measure and push variable complexity into helper measures excluded from the AI schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Subtly wrong filter context in generated queries.

rules.title: Data types are correct and consistent across tables
rules.requirement: Every AI-visible column must carry the correct data type - amounts as decimal, dates as date, identifiers as whole number - consistently across tables.
rules.rationale: Stated requirement with these exact examples. A numeric amount stored as text cannot be aggregated and the generator will not tell you why the answer is empty.

check.how: Run the Best Practice Analyzer data type rules across AI-visible columns.

rules.remediation: Fix types in Power Query or the source; do not paper over with DAX conversion in measures.
rules.impactIfViolated: Empty or wrong aggregations that look like missing data.

rules.title: Categorical values are standardized
rules.requirement: Values in AI-visible categorical columns must be standardized - Open, Closed, Pending - without mixed case, trailing whitespace, or synonym variants of the same state.
rules.rationale: Data consistency with standardized values is a stated requirement. Instance-value matching is literal; 'open', 'Open ' and 'OPEN' are three different filter targets.

check.how: Profile distinct values per AI-visible categorical column; flag case and whitespace variants of the same value.

rules.remediation: Normalize in the transformation layer and add a data quality test to keep it normalized.
rules.impactIfViolated: Filters match a subset of the rows they should, producing understated numbers that look valid.

rules.title: Format strings are set on AI-visible measures and columns
rules.requirement: Measures and columns must carry appropriate format strings, since format string is part of the grounding data.
rules.rationale: Format strings are listed among the semantic model properties supplied as grounding data in both the data-question and DAX query view paths. They tell the generator whether a number is currency, a percentage or a count.

check.how: List AI-visible measures and numeric columns with empty or default format strings.

rules.remediation: Set currency, percentage and precision formats explicitly.
rules.impactIfViolated: Percentages presented as raw decimals and currency without denomination.

rules.title: Data categories are set where they carry semantic meaning
rules.requirement: Columns representing geography, URLs, images or barcodes must have the appropriate data category set.
rules.rationale: Data category is explicitly part of the grounding data supplied to Copilot.

check.how: Check data category on geographic and URL columns in the AI schema.

rules.remediation: Set City, State/Province, Country and Postal Code categories on the relevant columns.
rules.impactIfViolated: Weaker map visual selection and geographic reasoning.

rules.title: High-cardinality columns are identified and justified
rules.requirement: High-cardinality columns must be identified with the Semantic Model Memory Analyzer and either removed, or justified and excluded from the AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Named as a target of analysis alongside incorrect data types and inefficient DAX. High cardinality drives both model size and the instance-value index budget.

check.how: Rank AI-visible columns by cardinality from a VPAX extract; review the top of the list for necessity.

rules.remediation: Remove, bucket, or exclude from the AI schema. A transaction ID needs no place in a natural-language surface.
rules.impactIfViolated: Index budget exhausted by columns nobody asks about, starving the ones they do.
